column6: Bullet 1 said every layout has a default; a forced active choice has none. Dropped "default", kept order and emphasis.

Bullet 3: opt-out consent is not "registration status"; now "counts everyone who has not opted out". Bullet 4: "most employees long after enrollment" overstated (copied from Explainer; persistence decays over years); now "many employees after enrollment". Older Explainer line 62 has the same "most" overstatement.
Bullet 4 "engages deliberation only when" is an absolute copied from Explainer; changed to "mainly when".

Bullet 2 defined saliency as "payoffs large enough to matter"; in Smith's precepts saliency means payoffs depend on decisions (size/override is dominance). Copied from the older Core Idea, which carries the same misdefinition.

Bullet 2 named "statisticians" as a group shown to persist in framing; not a citable finding (copied from older Q1 explanation). Now "physicians and other experts"; "both frames are shown" made precise as "same people answer both frames".
Bullet 3 second clause (payment can make the violation salient) is a hedged theoretical possibility, kept.
Bullet 3 attributed the expected-vs-unexpected price prediction to all reference-dependent models; status-quo-referenced models do not make it. Now "Expectations-based models such as Koszegi-Rabin".

Bullet 4 "people feel less regret for [inaction]" is too absolute (long-run regrets often concern inactions, Gilovich-Medvec); now "tend to expect less regret". Older Q0 explanation overstates Madrian-Shea ("years after", "no switching cost").

Bullet 3 "the patterns hold" at months-of-wages stakes is overstated (copied from Explainer): offers stay above minimum but rejection of a given low share falls as stakes rise (Slonim-Roth, Cameron, Andersen et al.). Older Explainer line 61 has the same overstatement.
